Builders can now call this full-duplex API model at $0.05 per active minute, ranking #1 on Jarvis Bench with 100% task completion when delegating to GPT 6.2 Sol Medium. Pairing #1 naturalness, delegated success, and clear pricing gives buyers a production baseline. Results rely on 2,442 Voice Arena votes and leave custom enterprise tools and noisy telephony unproven.

Vernier lets evaluators find the smallest reliable score gap on zero-shot time-series forecasting leaderboards, while OS-Omni tests computer-use agents on live long-horizon workflows across six platforms. items.title: Running native NVFP4 locally, evaluating agent APIs, training live harness adapters, and more
items.summary: Local inference takes a leap today as llama.cpp adds cross-platform NVFP4 support, Ollama brings Inkling 2 Mini to 32 GB desktops, and Hugging Face trains harness adapters live with public GGUFs. Meanwhile, NVIDIA opens a 3B-active autoregressive image model, Together AI ships Hurdle for API agent evals, and GPT 6.2 Astra Preview begins rolling out to Kiro Enterprise.
items.content_html:
Local inference takes a leap today as llama.cpp adds cross-platform NVFP4 support, Ollama brings Inkling 2 Mini to 32 GB desktops, and Hugging Face trains harness adapters live with public GGUFs. Meanwhile, NVIDIA opens a 3B-active autoregressive image model, Together AI ships Hurdle for API agent evals, and GPT 6.2 Astra Preview begins rolling out to Kiro Enterprise.

Sparse open-weight image generation gets cheaper to run with NVIDIA's Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B. Builders can now run a 30B autoregressive text-to-image model activating only 3B parameters per step. That sparse design lowers inference cost while keeping weights open. License terms, quality benchmarks, and hardware requirements are missing.

Local inference cuts conversion and runtime overhead on consumer hardware. In llama.cpp, Inkling 2 Mini now serves natively from its NVFP4 GGUF across Apple Silicon, CUDA, AMD, Windows, and Vulkan, while llm.asm runs Qwen3-0.6B in 12 KB of zero-dependency x86-64 assembly. Avoiding requantization preserves native accuracy, and stripping runtime and OS layers shows how much CPU decode speed can be recovered. llama.cpp lacks throughput and memory-bandwidth benchmarks, and llm.asm's speed claims are author-reported on x86-64 only.

Coding agents gain multi-repo scope as simulation testing moves to one standard. In T3 Code 0.1.12, one agent turn can now span several repositories, while Real2SimLab evaluates coding agents generating simulation programs from video on one platform. That removes manual switching across frontend, backend, and library repos, and makes simulation benchmarks comparable. T3 Code omits conflict handling, branch coordination, and context limits, and Real2SimLab offers only a paper summary without code or scores.

  2. llama.cpp adds NVFP4 support across Apple Silicon and GPUs (on Magpie): llama.cpp can now run NVFP4 weights natively across Apple Silicon, CUDA, AMD, Windows, and Vulkan, letting Inkling 2 Mini serve from its official GGUF without requantizing experts.
  3. llm.asm runs Qwen3-0.6B on bare metal in assembly (on Magpie): You can boot a 22 KB bare-metal OS or run Qwen3-0.6B inference in 12 KB of pure x86-64 NASM assembly with zero dependencies.
  4. T3 Code 0.1.12 spans multiple repos per agent turn (on Magpie): In T3 Code 0.1.12, one project and a single agent turn can now span several repositories at once.

items.title: Run a 27B coder in 5.9 GB, prove 9/4, slice Gemini files, and more
items.summary: The day mixes compact open weights with big research claims: a ternary 27B model, Baidu's open ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview, and OpenAI results in protein design and matrix multiplication. Google's Gemini API also got more practical for agents that handle documents, audio and video.
items.content_html:
The day mixes compact open weights with big research claims: a ternary 27B model, Baidu's open ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview, and OpenAI results in protein design and matrix multiplication. Google's Gemini API also got more practical for agents that handle documents, audio and video.

A 27B coding model now fits in 5.9 GB because its weights are ternary. That is small enough to try on an ordinary laptop or a cheap GPU, so a local coding agent no longer needs a large card. PrismML says it scores 75.6 on SWE-bench Verified. That figure comes from the vendor's own launch post, so test it on your own repos before you rely on it.

Baidu's open model takes the opposite route to efficiency, with 280B total parameters, only 14B active per token, and a 1M context. The Apache 2.0 license lets a company put it inside a commercial product without a custom deal. The long context suits whole-codebase or long-document work. It is a preview with no quality numbers given, so treat it as something to benchmark, not a proven pick.

A public preprint says an OpenAI model proved the matching lower bound that pins the matrix multiplication exponent at 2.25. Mathematicians can now check the argument line by line. If it holds, it settles a long open question and joins OpenAI's protein work, where designs showed binding across five targets, as a sign that general models can do frontier research. The proof still needs expert verification, and binding on five targets is not a usable drug.

items.summary: Open weights led the day: a sparse multimodal MoE for document and workflow work, and a tiny OCR model that runs on a single CPU core. items.content_html:
Open weights led the day: a sparse multimodal MoE for document and workflow work, and a tiny OCR model that runs on a single CPU core. Around them, coding agents proved useful as robot controllers, Anthropic claimed a Lean-checked VP not equal to VNP proof, and local Apple silicon inference got faster.

A document pipeline can now run on your own hardware, from page scan to agent action. LlamaIndex's open OCR model reads text and layout at about 426 ms per page on one CPU core, so ingestion needs no GPU or paid API. Ling-3.2-air can then reason over those documents and run workflow steps while activating only 5.5B of its 124B parameters per token, with day-0 vLLM support. Not yet shown: OCR accuracy against larger models, and an outside check of the team's AutomationBench-AA gain from 15.7% to 61%.

Anthropic says an internal Claude model produced a machine-checked proof that VP differs from VNP over every field. Anyone can inspect the 70-page paper and its Lean formalization instead of taking the claim on trust. If it holds, frontier math results may start arriving with proofs a computer has already checked. Expert review is not reported yet, and the result does not settle P vs NP.

The harness around a model is becoming the part teams tune. The robot policy study argues that interface design, not just model choice, decides whether a general model can control a robot, though its success rates are the authors' own and no code is linked. The backend switcher makes the same bet for coding agents, letting teams change the model under a tool without changing the tool, but its stars show interest, not output quality.

items.title: Robots write gripper code, GLM-5.4 leads open coding, llama.cpp fork speeds up, and more
items.summary: SenseTime put a 27B robot-manipulation vision-language model on Hugging Face, and an early review puts GLM-5.4 at the top of open coding models on one benchmark. Around them sit a faster llama.cpp fork, a tool for checking LLM server speed claims, agent GPU access through Colab, and a run of architecture papers on memory, diffusion language models and world models.
items.content_html:
SenseTime put a 27B robot-manipulation vision-language model on Hugging Face, and an early review puts GLM-5.4 at the top of open coding models on one benchmark. Around them sit a faster llama.cpp fork, a tool for checking LLM server speed claims, agent GPU access through Colab, and a run of architecture papers on memory, diffusion language models and world models.

A new paper gives world model builders a way to catch objects passing through each other without retraining the base model. Teams building interactive video world models can read hidden states from a frozen diffusion transformer to detect and reduce these physical violations. Clipping objects are one of the most visible failures in generated worlds, and a lightweight check costs far less than a new base model. It is a paper only, with no code or deployed results shown yet.

Clover tests a different route to language models, generating by diffusion instead of predicting the next token. Researchers describe a mixture-of-experts design with 35 billion total and 3 billion active parameters that supports thinking-mode generation, pairing recurrent memory of earlier context with block-level attention. For builders watching inference costs, the small active share is the part to track. No weights, speed or benchmark numbers are given, so its quality is unknown.

Agent tools covered in earlier editions keep gaining stars, which signals demand rather than new capability. The FFmpeg skill for coding agents added 3,748 stars this week, Alibaba's review bot added 3,700, and T3 Code drew 41,514 this month. Together they suggest builders want agents that edit video locally, review code with fixed rules alongside an LLM, and run from any device. items.content_html:
The day's clearest new capability is pi-H3, an open few-step distill of MiniMax H3 video generation with weights, code and a ComfyUI node. Around it sit local inference measurements, a tool for porting slow functions with a coding agent, and a run of research papers on robotics, navigation and spatial reasoning.

An open distill of MiniMax H3 now generates video in 2 to 4 steps with no VAE decoder. Weights, code, a demo Space and a ComfyUI node are all out, so few-step video can drop into existing workflows today. The author reports 768p video faster than real time on one B200 and under 40 s on one RTX 3090, but those are the author's own figures. NVIDIA's Posterior Matching Distillation points the same way for images by dropping auxiliary score networks, though only a paper summary is available.

A community quant fits Inkling-2-Mini in 5.4 GB of memory, far below the 17 to 18 GB 4-bit files. That could put the model on laptops and small GPUs that could not hold it before. Speed is a separate limit: the looped design reads about 5.5 GB per token, and earlier reports put a single Spark stream near 49 tok/s. The quant comes with no quality or speed numbers yet.

Builders can now have a coding agent port only the slow functions of a Python, Node or Ruby app. The tool profiles the app, rewrites the hot code and checks that it behaves the same, which is safer than a full rewrite. No measured speedups or production cases are stated.

items.content_html:
Open weights lead the day, with Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini showing up alongside quantized builds and a memory guide, plus new models from Apple and Tencent. AWS fills much of the rest with grounded document extraction and a KV caching skill, while new benchmarks rank frontier models on parsing, real robots, inference tuning and drug discovery.

Thinking Machines has put an open-weight 26B model that reads images and text within reach of a laptop. It is a looped mixture-of-experts design, and Unsloth's ready-made quantized files let you test it on modest hardware without converting the weights yourself. That makes private, offline prototyping of image and text workflows possible without a cloud bill. No benchmarks or license have been published, and the quality lost at each quantization level is not shown.

Apple's new depth model keeps metric depth from a single camera steady across the frames of a video. Teams training mixture-of-experts models now have an open guide built from about 800k GPU hours of another team's experiments. Most teams could not afford to learn these lessons on their own GPUs, so builders can now skip some costly failed runs. It reflects one team's experiments, so results on other clusters are not guaranteed.

ByteDance's Axion 1.0 suggests agent post-training can be much shorter and cheaper than many assumed. Its Apache 2.0 code and data let teams rerun a recipe of two supervised stages plus RL on about 18k samples, with the 35B supervised stage taking about 90 GPU-hours. Claude Code teams can now track AWS spending per developer across accounts. items.content_html:

Around them sit a laptop result on reading model weights, Tencent's Hy4 with vision, and identity plumbing for enterprise agents.

A 27B open model running on a laptop can now attempt the weight-reading task that a recent paper showed frontier models like GPT-6 Astra can do. Researchers can run inspection and editing experiments on raw weights without paying for a frontier API. Heretic, the training-free editing tool, picked up a Latent Space mention today, so teams now have local ways both to read weights and to change them. The weight-reading result rests on one blog test, with no systematic check of reliability.

The newest vLLM release serves four more models, adds speculative decoding options, and reports 1.5 to 2x faster decode on GB300. Teams can now serve Reflection Beam-1.0, Step-5 Preview, Nemotron Parse 3.5 and MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 from one stack. The catch is plumbing: wheels are CUDA 13.0 only and ROCm 10.0 is the default, so plan environment upgrades before moving. The speedups are vendor-reported and tied to that hardware.

Colibri's newest claim is that it runs 744B MoE models in about 10GB of RAM. If that holds, tiering experts across GPU, RAM and NVMe could put frontier-scale MoE models on hardware teams already own. The figure comes from a post on X, not a published benchmark, so test it on your own workloads first.

items.title: Prove inference, reuse KV caches, write weights, scale Git, and more
items.summary: The strongest new items are about trust and plumbing: proofs that a reply came from a committed model, wider prefix cache reuse in SGLang, and a Git backend built for agent-scale coding. Around them sit an experiment in LLMs editing weights directly, an open science model, and a batch of agent runtimes and patterns from Microsoft, Amp and AWS.
items.content_html:
The strongest new items are about trust and plumbing: proofs that a reply came from a committed model, wider prefix cache reuse in SGLang, and a Git backend built for agent-scale coding. Around them sit an experiment in LLMs editing weights directly, an open science model, and a batch of agent runtimes and patterns from Microsoft, Amp and AWS.

A model provider can now prove that a given reply came from the model it committed to, without revealing the weights. Anthropic's FlashProve lets anyone check that proof on an ordinary CPU in seconds, so a buyer could confirm which model actually served them. The result has been reproduced. The cost is high: making the proofs takes about 70 to 95 times the GPU time of plain inference, and it is not shown whether that overhead can come down enough for routine traffic.

SGLang can now reuse cached prompt prefixes even when serving is split across parallel and disaggregated setups. Reuse now works with context and pipeline parallelism, speculative decoding and prefill-decode disaggregation. On coding-agent traffic the cache hit rate went from 30% to 95%, with median time to first token under 3 seconds. Those figures come from one customer's workload, so other traffic may see different gains.

Coding agents are also straining source control, judging by how OpenAI rebuilt its Git backend for Codex. Pando stays Git-compatible while coping with the development volume Codex produces. Together with the SGLang result, it points to agent load as a planning problem for both serving and repositories. Pando is OpenAI's internal system, so teams can study the design but cannot run it.

  1. Mistral Large 4 still trending with its technical report (on Magpie): Mistral Large 4 is still drawing attention, with 1,522 Hugging Face likes and its technical report circulating alongside the open weights.
  2. OpenAI's Pando, a Git-compatible backend for Codex scale (on Magpie): Teams can study how OpenAI rebuilt its Git backend, Pando, to cope with the volume of development Codex produces.
  3. Astra: an LLM that reads and writes Qwen weights (on Magpie): Researchers can look at early evidence that an LLM can natively read and write neural network weights to improve a Qwen model.
  4. Anthropic's FlashProve: zero-knowledge proofs of LLM inference (on Magpie): A provider can commit to hidden weights and prove each reply came from that model, and anyone can check the proof on an ordinary CPU in seconds.
  5. SGLang HiCache reuses prefix cache across parallel serving (on Magpie): SGLang users can reuse prefix KV cache across context and pipeline parallelism, speculative decoding and prefill-decode disaggregation.

New possibility: Shared agent skill files become a serving cost lever, not just a style guide

items.title: Drive desktop apps via accessibility trees, run MiniMax locally, benchmark agents, and more
items.summary: Agent tooling leads the day: desktop control through OS accessibility trees, a 1.6T multimodal agent model from Meituan, and a hard new agent benchmark where the top score is 12.0. Running very large models on your own hardware also keeps getting easier, through community quants of MiniMax M3.1 Flash and disk-streamed MoE inference in pure C.
items.content_html:
Agent tooling leads the day: desktop control through OS accessibility trees, a 1.6T multimodal agent model from Meituan, and a hard new agent benchmark where the top score is 12.0. Running very large models on your own hardware also keeps getting easier, through community quants of MiniMax M3.1 Flash and disk-streamed MoE inference in pure C.

Agents can now work desktop apps by reading the structure the operating system already exposes, not by guessing from screenshots. Vercel's tool reads OS accessibility trees, gives each element a stable reference, and makes actions safe to retry. For teams automating client workflows, that should mean fewer misclicks and lower running costs than pixel-based control. The source offers no benchmark, so the reliability gain is still a claim, not a measurement.

Very large open models are moving onto hardware people already own, by two different routes. Community quants shrink MiniMax's 428B M3.1 Flash to a 2-bit file of 143.9 GB, with a recipe for a single DGX Spark. Colibri instead streams MoE experts from disk through a zero-dependency C engine, so the whole model never has to sit in memory. Both make on-premise use of 400B-class models more realistic, but the quality lost at 2-bit is unmeasured and Colibri publishes no speed numbers.

  1. Vercel's Agent Desktop drives apps through accessibility trees (on Magpie): Any agent can now operate desktop apps through their real UI structure from OS accessibility trees, with stable refs and retry-safe actions, instead of guessing from pixels.
  2. Colibri runs MoE models in pure C from disk (on Magpie): You can run large MoE models on hardware you already own with a zero-dependency C engine that streams experts from disk.
  3. Rea agent reverse engineering repo keeps trending (on Magpie): Nothing new since the 19 October write-up; it is still drawing attention with over 420,000 GitHub stars this month.
  4. Community quants run MiniMax M3.1 Flash on local hardware (on Magpie): You can run the 428B M3.1 Flash locally, including a 2-bit 143.9 GB quant and a recipe for a single DGX Spark.
  5. Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe 30B-A4B keeps trending (on Magpie): Nothing new since the 1 November write-up; it is still drawing attention, with 635 likes on Hugging Face and a ThursdAI mention.

items.title: DeepSeek agent works repos, Qwen teams beat Fable 5, agents write kernels, and more
items.summary: Agents moved further into real engineering work today: a proactive repo agent from DeepSeek, a team of small open models on a hard coding benchmark, and an agent swarm writing GPU kernels. Around them sit cheaper inference on AMD hardware, an open DNA training set with a full recipe, and new local tools for pooling GPUs and generating images and speech.
items.content_html:
Agents moved further into real engineering work today: a proactive repo agent from DeepSeek, a team of small open models on a hard coding benchmark, and an agent swarm writing GPU kernels. Around them sit cheaper inference on AMD hardware, an open DNA training set with a full recipe, and new local tools for pooling GPUs and generating images and speech.

Open models now look credible for hard coding work, both as coordinated teams and as agents that act inside a repo. Five open 27B Qwen models working through Memdoor's team-solve workflow beat Fable 5 on LiveCodeBench Hard, and the result was reproduced. DeepSeek's MIT-licensed prototype picks up issues and opens PRs in one GitHub repo without waiting for a prompt. The team result rests on one benchmark with no cost or latency figures, and the agent has no reliability data.

Anyone serving large agent models got two reasons to look past the newest GPUs. A vLLM agent swarm wrote about 10,000 lines of fused Hopper kernels that reportedly raise decode speed by up to 38%, stretching the life of older hardware. AMD reports an MI355X server with tuned kernels running Kimi K3 at up to 2x the performance per dollar of a B200, on one node. Both figures are reported, and the AMD result covers one model from one source.

Teams building DNA models now have an open dataset and a full training recipe to start from. FineDNA pairs genomic sequences and biology text with about 200k supervised samples and about 98k RL prompts. The recipe shows midtraining is what lets RL work on DNA tasks, a lesson for other domain models. Carbon-X results are team-reported.

  2. DeepSeek open-sources proactive repo coding agent prototype (on Magpie): You can run DeepSeek's MIT-licensed super-agent prototype, a proactive coding agent that works one GitHub repo through issues and PRs.
  3. Hugging Face releases FineDNA set and Carbon-X DNA model (on Magpie): You can train open DNA language models using FineDNA's genomic sequences, biology text, about 200k supervised samples and about 98k RL prompts, with the full Carbon recipe.
  4. Agent swarm writes Hopper kernels for faster decode (on Magpie): An agent swarm wrote about 10,000 lines of fused Hopper kernels that reportedly raise decode speed by up to 38%.
  5. AMD MI355X reaches 2x B200 cost efficiency on Kimi K3 (on Magpie): With AITER kernel tuning and MonoKernel decode, an MI355X server reportedly delivers up to 2x better performance per dollar than a B200 for agentic inference, keeping the model on one node.

items.title: Check a backdoored extension, pick Android Studio agents, run diffusion MoE locally, and more
items.summary: A backdoor in a Claude Code extension on the Cursor Marketplace leads a day built around coding agents, from 40-plus ACP agents in stable Android Studio to crash restarts in Cua and image generation in OpenCode. On the model side, Clover 35B A3B runs locally in preview, a 164MB speech model works on any CPU, and SGLang now serves 1.09 million tokens per second per GPU.
items.content_html:
A backdoor in a Claude Code extension on the Cursor Marketplace leads a day built around coding agents, from 40-plus ACP agents in stable Android Studio to crash restarts in Cua and image generation in OpenCode. On the model side, Clover 35B A3B runs locally in preview, a 164MB speech model works on any CPU, and SGLang now serves 1.09 million tokens per second per GPU.

Anyone who installed the Claude Code for VS Code extension from the Cursor Marketplace should check it now, because that listing carried a backdoor. Coding agent extensions read your code and act on your machine, so one bad listing is a direct supply chain risk. It is not yet known how many users were affected or how the backdoor got in.

Android teams face the same trust question on a wider scale, since stable Android Studio now lets them choose among about 40 ACP agents. Agents such as Claude Agent and Codex can reach the emulator, build system, Logcat and Compose Previews, so a team can standardize on one agent across tools. That broad access is also why vetting each agent's source matters. There is no evidence yet on agent quality inside the IDE.

Inference is getting cheaper from both ends, on shared servers and on local hardware. SGLang's peak throughput on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash rose from 654K to 1.09 million tokens per second per GPU in four days, though that is a vendor-run figure on one setup. Locally, you can test whether the Clover diffusion mixture-of-experts matches an autoregressive Qwen model, and transcribe English on any CPU at a 5.21% average word error rate. Both rest on thin evidence: one reviewer's test of a preview, and a model-card claim.

  3. SGLang hits 1.09M tokens per second per GPU (on Magpie): SGLang now serves DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at 1.09 million tokens per second per GPU peak total throughput, up from 654K four days earlier, and 943 tokens per second per user at concurrency 1.
  4. Clover 35B A3B diffusion MoE tested locally (on Magpie): You can run Clover 35B A3B, an open-weight diffusion mixture-of-experts model in preview, locally and compare it with an autoregressive Qwen model.
  5. Phonon-2 speech recognition fits in 164MB on CPU (on Magpie): You can run accurate English speech recognition on any CPU with a 164MB model that averages 5.21% word error rate on the Open ASR leaderboard's seven English sets.

items.title: Open Mistral Large 4, squeeze it to 1 bit, agent-tune kernels, and more
items.summary: Mistral's 1T-parameter open-weight model leads the day, with vLLM serving, Axolotl fine-tuning and an Unsloth 1-bit local quant landing around it. An agent that wrote a faster attention kernel, a large open robot dataset, agent-aware version control and new speech and audio models fill out the rest.
items.content_html:
Mistral's 1T-parameter open-weight model leads the day, with vLLM serving, Axolotl fine-tuning and an Unsloth 1-bit local quant landing around it. An agent that wrote a faster attention kernel, a large open robot dataset, agent-aware version control and new speech and audio models fill out the rest.

Mistral's 1T-parameter image-and-text model can be self-hosted, served and fine-tuned from the first day, and it even fits on one workstation. Teams can serve it in vLLM, LoRA fine-tune it in Axolotl, or test it privately on a Mac Studio with Unsloth's 223GB 1-bit quant. That puts frontier-scale work on infrastructure a client controls. Quality has not been independently benchmarked, and the 91% top-1 retention figure is Unsloth's own check.

An agent tuned GPU kernels well enough to rival expert libraries. OpenBMB's open harness lets an agent optimize kernels. Its fused prefill kernel ran in 472 microseconds against FlashMLA's 518, and it matched or beat 18 of 22 expert-library kernels. That could cut inference cost without hand-written CUDA, but it was one live run on one GPU type, so broad gains are unproven.

Large-scale speech recognition can now run offline from open weights. NVIDIA's 30B-A4B transcription model is on Hugging Face, which gives a local alternative to hosted transcription APIs. That matters to buyers with privacy or connectivity limits. No word error rates are given, so accuracy against hosted services is unknown.

  1. Mistral Large 4 open weights, 1T-A52B multimodal (on Magpie): You can download and self-host Mistral Large 4, a 1T-parameter image-and-text model, and serve it in vLLM or LoRA fine-tune it in Axolotl.
  2. ForgeKernel agent writes faster attention prefill kernel (on Magpie): You can use OpenBMB's open harness to have an agent optimize GPU kernels, and use its fused prefill kernel that ran 472 vs 518 microseconds against FlashMLA.
  3. Unsloth 1-bit GGUF runs Mistral Large 4 locally (on Magpie): You can run the 1T-parameter Mistral Large 4 on a Mac Studio using a 223GB 1-bit quant that keeps 91% of top-1 accuracy.
  4. NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe 30B-A4B speech model (on Magpie): You can run NVIDIA's 30B-A4B speech recognition model from open weights on Hugging Face, including offline.
  5. Zed DeltaDB links each code edit to its agent conversation (on Magpie): You can keep a Git-compatible history where every edit is tied to the agent conversation that produced it.

New possibility: Aggressive local quants need repetition-loop tests before they touch document pipelines
